correctness.rationale: For any projective plane q>=2, NN^T=qI+J and row sums q+1 give all heat matrix blocks by singular values d=q+1 and sqrt(q). The signed difference of incident point/line rows has masses +a,-b,+c and -a,+b,-c; positivity follows from convolution K(t)=integral_0^t sinh(sqrt q(t-u))/sqrt q exp(-du)du. The explicit edge-1-Lipschitz dual potential has value a+3qb+q²c; a matching primal coupling exists since outside-neighborhood incidence subgraph is q-regular bipartite. Edge-path triangle inequality gives full Lipschitz operator norm, regardless of Desarguesian or edge-transitivity assumptions. Derivative exponential polynomial yields unique positive-time peak and later 1 crossing, compact-uniform t=s/q limit e^-2s+4s e^-s with maximum 1.64046408905... . Independently built prime-field incidence matrices for q=2,3 and solved transport LPs at t=.08,.4,.9; all direct W1 values match formula to <1e-8. The general result relies on incidence axioms, not finite field tests.
